The invention relates to an air-guide member (100) for guiding an air flow (AF) in the food preparation chamber of an apparatus using the air flow (AF) to prepare food ingredients. The air-guide member (100) comprises a plurality of air-deflecting arms (101) arranged symmetrically and extending in a horizontal plane (P) between an inner part (IP) and an outer part (OP) of the air-guide member (100). The air-deflecting arms (101) comprises a first surface (S1) being inclined with a positive angle compared to the horizontal plane (P), and a second surface (S2) being inclined with a negative angle compared to the horizontal plane (P). The air-deflecting arms (101) is such that the second surface (S2) of a given air-deflecting arms (101) and the first surface (SI) of an air-deflecting arms (101) consecutive to the given air-deflecting arms (101) intersect to form a concave air channel (AC) extending between the outer part (OP) and the inner part (IP). This allows directing the air flow upwards and more evenly between the outer part and the inner part of the air-guide. The food ingredients can thus receive a flow of hot air having a more uniform air pressure distribution, which results in a more even cooking of the food ingredients.

The invention relates to an air-guide member for directing airflow within the food preparation chamber of an apparatus that cooks food ingredients using circulating air, such as a hot-air cooking appliance.

The air-guide member is designed to influence and control the movement of air inside the food preparation chamber. It includes a plurality of air-deflecting arms that are arranged symmetrically around the member. These air-deflecting arms extend generally horizontally between an inner part and an outer part of the air-guide member, forming a structured airflow-guiding arrangement.

Each air-deflecting arm is shaped to redirect the flow of air in a desired manner. In particular, each arm includes a first surface that is inclined at a positive angle relative to a horizontal plane, and a second surface that is inclined at a negative angle relative to the horizontal plane. This configuration gives the arms a profiled shape that helps guide and deflect the air as it passes through the food preparation chamber.

The adjacent air-deflecting arms define concave air channels between them. These concave air channels extend from the outer part of the air-guide member toward the inner part, or vice versa, depending on the direction of airflow within the apparatus. Because of their concave shape and orientation, the channels help collect, guide, and redirect the airflow in a controlled manner.

During operation of the cooking apparatus, hot air is circulated through the food preparation chamber. As the air encounters the air-guide member, the inclined surfaces of the air-deflecting arms and the concave air channels cooperate to direct the airflow upward and distribute it more evenly throughout the chamber. This improved airflow distribution reduces localized hot or cold zones and helps ensure that the food ingredients are exposed to a more uniform stream of hot air.

As a result, the air-guide member contributes to more even heating and more uniform cooking of the food ingredients. The improved circulation of hot air can enhance cooking performance, reduce the need for manual shaking or turning of the food, and improve the consistency of the final cooked product.
outputs.L4:
An air-guide member for a food preparation chamber is provided to improve the circulation of hot air during cooking. The air-guide member is positioned so that air flowing within the chamber is redirected in a controlled manner from an outer region of the chamber toward an inner region. In this way, the member helps guide heated air to the area where food ingredients are located, thereby supporting more effective heat transfer.

The air-guide member includes a plurality of air-deflecting arms arranged symmetrically with respect to a central region. Each air-deflecting arm has at least one inclined air-guiding surface. The inclined surfaces of adjacent or opposing arms are arranged in opposite directions, so that they cooperate to define concave air channels. These concave air channels receive air moving along the outer part of the chamber and direct the air inward and upward.

Because the air-deflecting arms are symmetrically arranged, the airflow is distributed in a balanced manner around the chamber. The oppositely inclined surfaces help reduce uneven flow patterns and prevent hot air from concentrating in only one area. Instead, the air is progressively guided toward the center and lifted upward, allowing the heated air to pass more uniformly through or around the food ingredients.

This configuration improves the pressure distribution within the food preparation chamber. By guiding the hot air from the outer part toward the inner part and directing it upward, the air-guide member promotes a more even circulation path. As a result, temperature differences within the chamber can be reduced, and food ingredients can be cooked more uniformly.

The air-guide member is particularly suitable for use in hot-air cooking appliances, such as air fryers, convection ovens, or similar food preparation devices. Its structure can help improve cooking performance without requiring a more complex fan system or additional heating elements. Through the use of symmetrical air-deflecting arms and concave air-guiding channels, the member provides a simple and effective way to enhance airflow control and achieve more consistent cooking results.

**The Power of “The” and “This”**

“The” and “this” are small words, but they play an important role in English. **“The”** is used to talk about something specific or already known. For example, when we say *the book*, we mean a particular book, not just any book. It helps give clarity and direction in a sentence.

**“This”** is also used to point to something specific, but it often refers to something close to the speaker or something currently being discussed. For example, *this idea* means the idea we are focusing on right now. It can make writing feel more immediate and connected.

Together, “the” and “this” help language become more precise. They guide the reader or listener, showing which object, idea, or situation is being mentioned. Although they are simple words, they are essential for clear communication.

counterfactuals.output: An air-guide member for a hot-air food preparation apparatus is provided. Each deflecting arm includes an inclined deflecting surface configured to guide a circulating hot-air flow outwardly and/or upwardly within a food preparation chamber. Concave air-guiding channels are formed between adjacent deflecting arms, the channels being configured to receive and redirect the hot air in a controlled flow pattern. The symmetrical arrangement of the deflecting arms and the inclined and concave guide surfaces promote a more uniform distribution of hot air through the apparatus, reducing localized high-velocity regions and stagnant zones. As a result, food items supported in the preparation chamber are exposed to more even airflow and heat transfer, thereby improving cooking uniformity.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft the “summary of the invention” section for a patent application about an air fryer air-flow guide with arms extending between inner and outer parts, where adjacent inclined surfaces form concave channels that direct hot air upward evenly.
counterfactuals.output:
## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to an air-flow guide for an air fryer, and more particularly to an air-flow guiding structure configured to distribute heated air in an upward direction in a more uniform manner within a cooking chamber.

In one aspect, an air-flow guide for an air fryer is provided. The air-flow guide may include an inner part, an outer part spaced radially outward from the inner part, and a plurality of arms extending between the inner part and the outer part. Each arm may include one or more inclined surfaces. Adjacent inclined surfaces of neighboring arms may cooperate to define concave air-flow channels. The concave air-flow channels are configured to guide hot air upwardly from a lower region of the air fryer toward food supported in the cooking chamber, thereby improving uniformity of air distribution and heating.

In another aspect, the plurality of arms may be arranged circumferentially between the inner part and the outer part. Each arm may extend generally radially, spirally, arcuately, or in another suitable direction between the inner and outer parts. The inclined surfaces of the arms may be angled relative to a horizontal plane, vertical axis, radial direction, circumferential direction, or a combination thereof, so as to impart an upward guiding component to air passing through or across the air-flow guide.

In some embodiments, the concave channels may be formed by opposing inclined side surfaces of adjacent arms. The channels may have a trough-like, curved, V-shaped, U-shaped, or otherwise recessed configuration when viewed in cross-section. The concave shape may collect, redirect, or smooth the flow of heated air and reduce localized turbulence or uneven flow concentration. As a result, hot air may be directed upward through multiple distributed channels to provide more even cooking of food positioned above the air-flow guide.

In some embodiments, the inner part may define a central opening, hub, ring, plate, or mounting portion. The outer part may define an annular ring, frame, peripheral wall, or support portion. The arms may be integrally formed with the inner part and the outer part, or may be separately formed and coupled thereto. The air-flow guide may be positioned below a food basket, tray, grill plate, or other food-supporting member of the air fryer.

In another aspect, an air fryer is provided that includes a housing defining a cooking chamber, a heating element, a fan configured to circulate heated air within the cooking chamber, and an air-flow guide disposed in an air-flow path of the heated air. The air-flow guide includes an inner part, an outer part, and a plurality of arms extending between the inner part and the outer part. Adjacent inclined surfaces of the arms form concave channels configured to direct hot air upward substantially evenly toward food in the cooking chamber.

In some embodiments, the air-flow guide may be disposed below the food-supporting member and above a lower wall of the cooking chamber. Heated air driven by the fan may travel along or beneath the air-flow guide and then be redirected upward by the inclined surfaces and concave channels. The arrangement may promote substantially uniform upward flow over a cooking area, thereby reducing hot spots, cold spots, or uneven browning.

In further embodiments, the width, depth, curvature, inclination angle, spacing, number, or angular distribution of the arms and concave channels may be selected to control air-flow velocity, pressure distribution, and upward flow direction. The arms may be symmetrically arranged about a central axis or may be asymmetrically arranged to compensate for fan location, heater configuration, chamber geometry, or other flow characteristics.

In yet another aspect, the invention provides an air-flow guide that is simple in structure, suitable for manufacture by molding, stamping, casting, machining, additive manufacturing, or other forming processes, and capable of improving cooking performance without requiring substantial modification of the air fryer housing, fan, or heating element.

Accordingly, the air-flow guide of the present invention can guide heated air upward through distributed concave channels formed between adjacent inclined surfaces, thereby improving the evenness of hot-air delivery to food and enhancing cooking uniformity in an air fryer.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical description of an invention: an air-guide member (100) in a food preparation chamber, with air-deflecting arms (101), surfaces S1 and S2 angled relative to a horizontal plane P, and air channels AC improving air pressure distribution.
counterfactuals.output:
An air-guide member (100) for use in a food preparation chamber is configured to influence and distribute a circulating air flow within the chamber. The air-guide member (100) comprises a body portion arranged in or adjacent to an air-flow path of the food preparation chamber and a plurality of air-deflecting arms (101) extending from the body portion.

Each air-deflecting arm (101) includes at least two air-guiding surfaces, including a first surface S1 and a second surface S2. The first surface S1 and the second surface S2 are arranged at respective angles relative to a horizontal reference plane P of the food preparation chamber. In particular, the surfaces S1 and S2 may be inclined differently with respect to the horizontal plane P so as to redirect air in selected directions within the chamber. The angular configuration of the surfaces S1, S2 promotes controlled deflection of the air flow, reduces localized high-velocity zones, and assists in directing air toward regions of the food preparation chamber that would otherwise receive reduced air flow.

The air-deflecting arms (101) are spaced from one another so as to define air channels AC between adjacent arms. The air channels AC provide guided flow passages through and/or around the air-guide member (100). During operation, air driven by a fan or other air-moving device passes through the air channels AC and is deflected by the surfaces S1 and S2. The combination of the inclined surfaces and the air channels AC improves distribution of air pressure within the food preparation chamber by reducing pressure imbalances and promoting a more uniform flow field.

In one implementation, the air-guide member (100) is positioned between an air inlet region and a cooking volume of the food preparation chamber. The air channels AC meter and direct the incoming air flow, while the angled surfaces S1 and S2 impart lateral and/or vertical components to the flow. As a result, heated air can be distributed more evenly around food items placed in the chamber, improving cooking uniformity, reducing hot spots, and enhancing thermal transfer efficiency.

The air-guide member (100) may be formed as a single molded, cast, stamped, or additively manufactured component, for example from a heat-resistant polymer, metal, or composite material suitable for exposure to elevated temperatures and cooking vapors. The geometry, number, spacing, and angular orientation of the air-deflecting arms (101), surfaces S1 and S2, and air channels AC may be selected according to the size and shape of the food preparation chamber and the desired air-flow characteristics.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, how an air-guide member for a food cooking appliance can guide airflow more uniformly by using multiple symmetrical arms with intersecting inclined surfaces forming concave air channels.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, an air-guide member for a food cooking appliance is configured to distribute a flow of heated air substantially uniformly within a cooking chamber. The air-guide member comprises a central body portion and a plurality of guide arms extending outwardly from the central body portion in a substantially symmetrical arrangement about a central axis of the air-guide member. Each guide arm includes at least two inclined guide surfaces arranged to intersect one another along a longitudinal region of the respective guide arm, thereby defining a generally concave air-guiding channel.

The inclined guide surfaces of each guide arm are oriented such that air impinging upon the air-guide member is divided and redirected along the concave air-guiding channels toward different circumferential regions of the cooking chamber. Because the guide arms are symmetrically distributed, the air flow is split into a plurality of substantially balanced flow paths. The intersecting inclined surfaces cooperate to reduce localized high-velocity streams and to guide the air outwardly and circumferentially in a controlled manner, thereby promoting a more even air velocity distribution and temperature distribution around food received in the cooking chamber.

In certain embodiments, the plurality of guide arms may be arranged radially, for example in pairs disposed opposite one another with respect to the central axis. Each guide arm may have a generally V-shaped, trough-shaped, or concavely recessed cross-section formed by the intersecting inclined surfaces. The concave air channels may extend from an inner region adjacent the central body portion toward an outer peripheral region of the air-guide member, so that air discharged from a fan or heating assembly is progressively guided outwardly. The inclined surfaces may be substantially planar, curved, or partially curved, and may be configured with substantially equal inclination angles on opposite sides of each channel to maintain symmetry of the guided air flow.

By forming multiple concave air channels in a symmetrical pattern, the air-guide member reduces turbulent concentration at a single discharge region and assists in distributing heated air over a wider angular range. Accordingly, the air-guide member improves cooking uniformity, reduces temperature gradients within the cooking chamber, and enhances consistent heating or crisping of food supported therein.
